What do you think the future of culture is, within, say, the next two centuries? How will future business models operate-- will the current dominate one always be used or will it be replaced? More centralization? Decentralization? What will the value and nature of culture in the future? What trends will continue?

Culture is a result of spontaneous orders, and therefore inherently unpredictible. The very best you can do is predict general trends based on the past, but it doesn't really help to envision what's actually going to happen.

For instance, some strains of culture will, due to circumstances of the moment, centralize. Then, those with an investment in the centralization will fight tooth and claw to keep it that way, and more so. If they win, their strain will possibly flourish for a while, but then wither and die as something else not predicted rises to take its place.

Look at music. The recording industry arose due to new technology, and the cost of it forced centralization. People within it viewed each new advance in tech as either a way to force more centralization, or a threat to the very industry itself. And it's immolating now, as various indie artists arise in fits and starts.

Or look at Hollywood. In the late 1960s, the "film school brats" cheered on the demise of the studio system, envisioning a utopia of auteurs getting no-strings-attached funding for art films, forever and ever, amen. According to Peter Biskind's book Easy Riders, Raging Bulls, Dennis Hopper sneered at George Cukor at a party in 1969 that his generation was going to bury everyone older. Didn't take six years before Spielberg's Jaws set the new blockbuster model, which Star Wars further refined, and the studios reframed their business models more and more toward that every year.

Sooner or later the mega-budget tentpole strategy is going to take a studio down, maybe several, though it doesn't look to be soon. After that, who knows what, exactly, will arise to take its place? Will Netflix and streaming in general be the source of most longform drama? Hell if I know. Might be something we haven't quite got just yet.

But people will keep making culture, because it's what human beings do. And the more people make, the more chances that one will hit upon the Next Big Thing.
